questions.question: Dr. Soulami practices as a natural person. According to the General Tax Code, his professional income falls under which category of personal income tax?
questions.explanation: Liberal professions, including dentists, generate Non-Commercial Profits (BNC) under the General Tax Code.

questions.question: In 2026, what is the maximum marginal rate of Personal Income Tax (PIT) in Morocco for a dentist practicing as a natural person?
questions.explanation: The progressive PIT scale applies with a marginal rate of 37% for the taxable net income bracket exceeding 180,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an annual turnover of 600,000 DH. Which tax regime is he automatically subject to?
questions.explanation: RNR is the default regime for liberal professions whose annual turnover exceeds 500,000 DH.

questions.question: What is the turnover threshold not to exceed for a dentist to opt for the Simplified Net Income regime (RNS)?
questions.explanation: RNS is an intermediate regime for liberal professions whose annual turnover does not exceed 500,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Soulami starts his activity in 2026. For how many months is he exempt from the Minimum Contribution (CM)?
questions.explanation: New taxpayers operating as individuals benefit from an exemption from the minimum contribution for the first 36 months of activity.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani, a natural person, has a turnover of 800,000 DH. What is the minimum amount of his Minimum Contribution (CM)?
questions.explanation: For natural persons subject to PIT, the minimum contribution cannot be less than 1,500 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has a turnover of 800,000 DH and a taxable income of 100,000 DH. Which tax will he pay if the CM is higher than the calculated PIT?
options: The income tax calculated on 100,000 DH
The higher amount between PIT and CM
No tax because the profit is low
questions.explanation: The taxpayer pays the higher amount between the calculated PIT and the CM. The CM for a natural person is 6% of turnover.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani, a natural person, has a turnover of 800,000 DH. What is the applicable Minimum Contribution (CM) rate?
questions.explanation: The CM rate for liberal professions operating as individuals is 6% of turnover.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the PIT exemption threshold for a single dentist with no dependents?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law maintains the taxable net income exemption threshold at 40,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Soulami wishes to opt for RNR even though his turnover is 300,000 DH. Is this possible?
options: Yes, opting for RNR is voluntary even below the thresholds
No, RNR is mandatory above 500,000 DH
Yes, but only with tax authority approval
No, RNS is imposed below 500,000 DH
questions.explanation: Any taxpayer may voluntarily opt for RNR, even if their turnover is below the regulatory thresholds.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has a tax deficit of 50,000 DH from his activity. Under the RNR regime, over how many years can he carry forward this deficit?
questions.explanation: Under RNR, the deficit can be carried forward against profits of the following four years.

questions.question: What is the particularity of the Single Professional Contribution (CPU) compared to RNR and RNS?
options: It allows deduction of all actual expenses
It offers a flat-rate tax of 10% on a flat-rate profit
It is exclusive to liberal professions
questions.explanation: CPU offers a flat-rate tax at 10% applied to a flat-rate profit calculated on turnover, without deduction of actual expenses.

questions.question: According to the progressive scale, what is the PIT rate applicable to the income bracket between 60,001 and 180,000 DH?
questions.explanation: The progressive PIT scale provides a rate of 34% for the taxable net income bracket between 60,001 and 180,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Soulami is considering creating an LLC for his practice. Which tax will the company be subject to?
questions.explanation: A company (LLC, SARLAU, SAS) is subject to Corporate Income Tax (CIT).

questions.question: In 2026, what is the CIT rate applicable to the profit bracket of 0 to 300,000 DH for an LLC?
questions.explanation: The progressive CIT scale provides a rate of 10% for the net taxable profit bracket between 0 and 300,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an LLC with a profit of 500,000 DH. What is the CIT rate applicable to the profit bracket between 300,001 and 1,000,000 DH?
questions.explanation: The progressive CIT scale provides a rate of 20% for the net taxable profit bracket between 300,001 and 1,000,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC with a net profit after CIT of 400,000 DH which he distributes as dividends. What is the withholding tax rate on these dividends?
questions.explanation: Dividend distribution is subject to a 10% withholding tax (WHT).

questions.question: From what profit level does CIT generally become more advantageous than PIT from a strictly tax perspective?
questions.explanation: The tipping point is around 200,000 to 250,000 DH of net profit, where CIT begins to be more advantageous than PIT.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an LLC. What is the minimum Minimum Contribution (CM) due by his company?
questions.explanation: For companies subject to CIT, the minimum contribution cannot be less than 3,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC created in 2026. For how many months is it exempt from the Minimum Contribution (CM)?
questions.explanation: Newly created companies benefit from an exemption from the CM for their first 36 months of activity.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an LLC with a turnover of 1,000,000 DH. What is the amount of his Minimum Contribution (CM) at the standard rate?
questions.explanation: The standard CM rate is 0.25% of turnover, i.e. 2,500 DH. Since the floor is 3,000 DH, this amount is due.

questions.question: According to the GTC, dental care procedures are generally:
questions.explanation: Dental care procedures are generally exempt from VAT, although aesthetic procedures may be subject to VAT.

questions.question: Dr. Soulami practices as a natural person. He may deduct the following expenses from his income, except:
options: The purchase costs of his personal vehicle for private use
questions.explanation: Only expenses incurred for professional activity are deductible. Expenses for a vehicle for private use are not deductible.

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an LLC with a profit of 2,000,000 DH. What is the CIT rate applicable to the profit bracket exceeding 1,000,000 DH?
questions.explanation: The progressive CIT scale provides a rate of 35% for the net taxable profit bracket exceeding 1,000,000 DH.

questions.question: What is the main difference between RNR and RNS in terms of accounting?
options: RNR requires full accounting, RNS requires simplified accounting
RNR does not require accounting, RNS requires full accounting
RNR requires simplified accounting, RNS requires no accounting
questions.explanation: RNR requires full accounting compliant with CGNC, while RNS uses simplified accounting.
